'''Suwa Gorōnin''' (諏訪御料人, 1530 – December 18, 1555) was a concubine of [[Takeda Shingen]]{{efn|Japanese feudal lord (1521–1573)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeda Shingen|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Takeda Harunobu) and the mother of {{ill|Takeda Katsuyori|en|Takeda Katsuyori|qid=Q662482|lt=Takeda Katsuyori}}. She was the daughter of {{ill|Suwa Yorishige|ja|諏訪頼重|ko|스와 요리시게|nl|Suwa Yorishige|qid=Q1213900|lt=Suwa Yorishige}}, the head of the {{ill|Suwa clan|de|Suwa (Klan)|fa|خاندان سووا|fr|Clan Suwa|id|Klan Suwa|it|Clan Suwa|ja|諏訪氏|ko|스와씨|pt|Clã Suwa|ru|Сува (род)|qid=Q2975376|lt=Suwa clan}}, and his concubine from the {{ill|Omi clan (麻績氏)|ja|小見氏}} (Omishi). Known also as "Taikata-sama," her actual name remains unknown. In historical sources, she is referred to as "Suwa Gorōnin" or "Suwa Gozen," both terms indicating a noblewoman.

== Biography ==
Suwa Gorōnin's birth year is uncertain, but according to the ''{{ill|Kōyō Gunkan|en|Kōyō Gunkan|qid=Q586111|lt=Kōyō Gunkan}}'', she became a concubine of Takeda Shingen at age 14 in 1545, suggesting she was born in 1530.<ref name="hira23">{{Cite book|author=平山優|title=長篠合戦と武田勝頼 敗者の日本史9|publisher=吉川弘文館|year=2014|page=23}}</ref><ref name="shiba476">{{Cite book|author=柴辻俊六|title=武田氏家臣団人名辞典|publisher=東京堂出版|year=2015|page=476}}</ref> ''Kōyō Gunkan'' praises her beauty, calling her a "notable beauty."<ref name="shiba476" />

At the time of her father Suwa Yorishige's leadership, the Suwa clan was allied with the {{ill|Takeda clan|en|Takeda clan|qid=Q1210114|lt=Takeda clan}}. Yorishige married {{ill|Nene Goryōnin|ja|禰々|lt=Neene}}, Takeda Shingen's half-sister, to strengthen the alliance. However, in 1541, after Shingen ousted his father {{ill|Takeda Nobutora|de|Takeda Nobutora|fa|تاکدا نوبوتورا|fr|Takeda Nobutora|it|Takeda Nobutora|ja|武田信虎|kk|Тэкада Нобутара|ko|다케다 노부토라|nl|Takeda Nobutora|no|Takeda Nobutora|ru|Такэда Нобутора|tr|Takeda Nobutora|uk|Такеда Нобутора|wuu|武田信虎|zh|武田信虎|qid=Q1192628|lt=Takeda Nobutora}}, Yorishige aligned with the {{ill|Uesugi clan|en|Uesugi clan|qid=Q1150058|lt=Uesugi clan}}, violating the Takeda-Suwa alliance. This led to Takeda's invasion of Suwa, resulting in the fall of the Suwa clan and Yorishige's forced seppuku.

To consolidate his control, Shingen took Suwa Gorōnin as a concubine and planned to have their son, Katsuyori, inherit the Suwa clan's legacy.<ref name="hira23" /> She is believed to have entered the Takeda household around 1545, residing at the {{ill|Tsutsujigasaki Castle|en|Tsutsujigasaki Castle|qid=Q11637200|lt=Tsutsujigasaki Mansion}}.<ref name="shiba476" />

Suwa Gorōnin died on November 6, 1555. Her grave is located at {{ill|Kenpuku-ji|ja|建福寺}} in present-day {{ill|Ina, Nagano|en|Ina, Nagano|qid=Q840888|lt=Ina, Nagano}}. Her Buddhist name was recorded as "Kenpukuji-dono Baigan Myōkō Daizenni."<ref name="shiba476" /> Another memorial exists at {{ill|Kannon-in (Okaya City)|ja|観音院 (岡谷市)}} in {{ill|Okaya, Nagano|en|Okaya, Nagano|qid=Q838672|lt=Okaya, Nagano}}, but it was constructed after her death based on fictional accounts.

== Influence and Legacy ==
According to ''{{ill|Tetsuzan-shū|ja|鉄山集}}'' and ''Butsugan Zenji Goroku,'' her son Katsuyori performed rituals in her memory, including the 17th death anniversary ceremony in 1571.<ref name="shiba476" />

There is speculation that she was adopted by {{ill|Netsu Motonao|ja|禰津元直}} to avoid her identity as a former enemy's daughter. This adoption would mean Katsuyori and {{ill|Takeda Nobukiyo|ja|武田信清|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeda Nobukiyo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q6639853}} were both her children, suggesting she lived until the 1560s.

== Cultural Impact ==
Suwa Gorōnin is often depicted as Takeda Shingen's favorite concubine, although this characterization is debated among historians. Historical dramas and novels have contributed to this portrayal, such as {{ill|Jirō Nitta|en|Jirō Nitta|qid=Q3179274|lt=Jirō Nitta}}'s ''{{ill|Takeda Shingen (novel)|ja|Takeda Shingen (小説)}}'', where she is called "Koi-hime," and {{ill|Yasushi Inoue|en|Yasushi Inoue|qid=Q712734|lt=Yasushi Inoue}}'s ''{{ill|The Samurai Banner of Furin Kazan|ja|風林火山 (小説)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fūrin Kazan (novel)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11665512}}'', where she is named "Yūbu-hime." 

The annual {{ill|Shingen-ko Festival|en|Shingen-ko Festival|qid=Q3562464|lt=Shingen-kō Festival}} in {{ill|Kōfu|en|Kōfu|qid=Q201932|lt=Kōfu, Yamanashi}} features a "Koi-hime Contest," adding to her legacy in popular culture.

== Depictions in Media ==
Suwa Gorōnin has been portrayed under various names in films and television dramas:
* ''{{ill|Samurai Banners|en|Samurai Banners|qid=Q2712195|lt=Fūrin Kazan (movie)}}'' as Yūbu-hime (1969, Toho, actress: {{ill|Yoshiko Sakuma|en|Yoshiko Sakuma|qid=Q11382739|lt=Yoshiko Sakuma}})
* ''{{ill|Takeda Shingen (1988 TV series)|ja|Takeda Shingen (NHK大河ドラマ)}}'' as Koi-hime (1988, NHK Taiga Drama, actress: {{ill|Yoko Minamino|en|Yoko Minamino|qid=Q456207|lt=Yōko Minamino}})
* ''{{ill|Fūrin Kazan (TV series)|en|Fūrin Kazan (TV series)|qid=Q843000|lt=Fūrin Kazan (NHK Taiga Drama)}}'' as Yūbu-hime (2007, NHK Taiga Drama, actress: {{ill|Yuki Shibamoto|en|Yuki Shibamoto|qid=Q9036475|lt=Kō Shibamoto}})
